english.title: Without authority sell an Olympic games ticket
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) sold a ticket for the

(A)_[London Olympic Games]_
(B)_[London Paralympic Games]_

(C)_[in a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..),]_
(D)_[in the course of a business, namely **(..SPECIFY THE BUSINESS..),]_

otherwise than in accordance with a written authorisation issued by the London Organising Committee
english.legislation: Contrary to section 31(1) and (6) of the London Olympic Games and Paralympic Games Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 31(3) of the London Olympic Games and Paralympic Games Act 2006 provides that a person does not commit this offence by advertising that a ticket is available for purchase if:-
(a) the sale of the ticket if purchased would be in the course of a business only by reason of section 31(2)(c), and (b) the person does not know, and could not reasonably be expected to discover, that section 31(2)(c) would apply to the sale.
(ii) Section 31(4) of the London Olympic Games and Paralympic Games Act 2006 provides that a person does not commit this offence (whether actual or inchoate) only by virtue of making facilities available in connection with electronic communication or the storage of electronic data.
(iii) Penalty increased from 14/02/12 to £20,000 by the London Olympic Games and Paralympic Games (Amendment) Act 2011.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding £20,000.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
